title: Asymptotic Pseudospectra in Dissipative Floquet Quantum Systems: Geometric Structures and Observable Dynamics
authors: Yuncheng Xie, Haozhe Shi, Zhuocheng Ma, Weibin Chu, Xin-Gao Gong
abstract: In periodically driven open quantum systems, nonnormality renders the Floquet spectrum insufficient as the system approaches the thermodynamic limit, so that pseudospectra are needed to characterize the dynamics accurately. While conventional approaches mainly focus on the local dynamics of isolated pseudospectra, their global connections and the resulting physical consequences for observables have remained largely unexplored. Here, we uncover this collective behavior by classifying the unit disk into distinct domains of exponential, algebraic, and bounded accuracy according to the asymptotic size-scaling laws of pseudospectral residuals, yielding an underlying geometric structure. We demonstrate the physical implications of this structure through two exactly solvable models. First, in a dissipative shift chain, parameter tuning drives geometric transitions that are detectable via spin-wave observables. Second, in a chiral XY model, we use this geometric structure to explain the origin of a measurable phenomenon: two correlation signals exchange their retention order under continuous parameter tuning. Our findings not only establish a new theoretical paradigm for understanding dissipative Floquet quantum systems, but also predict geometry-driven observables for quantum computing experiments.
summary: This paper develops a novel 'asymptotic pseudospectral atlas' to analyze open quantum systems driven by periodic forces, where standard spectral methods fail. By classifying the geometry of the pseudospectra, the authors predict that global structural changes in this atlas correspond directly to measurable physical events, such as the exchange of correlation signal orders in the chiral XY model.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitations of the Floquet spectrum for periodically driven open quantum systems, necessitating the use of pseudospectra to accurately characterize dynamics in the thermodynamic limit.
main_result: The authors establish an 'asymptotic pseudospectral atlas' that provides a geometric structure classifying the validity regimes (exponential, algebraic, bounded) of approximate modes, which dictates observable physical transitions.
method: The core method involves analyzing the asymptotic size-scaling laws of pseudospectral residuals, formalizing this into an atlas that partitions the unit disk into distinct geometric domains.
model_or_system: The study applies to general periodically driven open quantum systems, demonstrated using specific models like a dissipative shift chain and the chiral XY model.
key_observables: Spin-wave observables, correlation signals, and the pseudospectral residual $\epsilon_N(z)$ are used to detect geometric transitions.
important_parameters: The key parameters include the driving strength ($g$) and the system size ($N$), which govern the transitions between different scaling regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the 'common-limit hypothesis' for simplifying the asymptotic indices and involves complex block constructions for error bounding.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the pseudospectral atlas, showing how components merge and holes close at critical parameter values ($g_1, g_2$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the pseudospectral problem to introducing the asymptotic atlas, then applies this geometric framework to analyze specific physical models (dissipative shift chain, chiral XY model) to predict observable changes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, geometry-based theoretical tool to predict observable changes in complex, non-Hermitian, open quantum systems, linking spectral theory directly to measurable physical phenomena.
